taxonomyNote: NatureServe: C. leuconotus and C. mesoleucus were formerly separate species; Wozencraft (2005) included mesoleucus in C. leuconotus.
fieldMarks: Single white stripe from the top of the head, wedge-shaped at the start, to the tail tip; some northwestern animals have more white
Large naked snout resembling a hog's; small eyes and nose relative to the snout
Short coarse fur; tail mostly white above
Stocky legs; front claws larger for digging
Males average about 577 mm total length, females about 542 mm
behavior: Mostly nocturnal, sometimes active by day especially in winter; active year round
Feeds mainly on insects, especially larvae; digs and roots with snout and long claws, overturning rocks and logs
Dens in rock crevices, hollow logs, burrows, caves, mine shafts, woodrat houses or under buildings
habitat: Woodlands, grasslands, deserts, brushy areas and rocky canyons; most common in very rocky mountainous terrain.
range: Southwestern US south to northern Nicaragua. In the US: southeastern Colorado, extreme northwestern Oklahoma, Arizona, New Mexico and western Texas.
